title: field
content_html:
field

In field I and grid fields, a mark belongs to a larger area. The marks around it, the edges and the quieter parts of the image all affect how it reads. A field of view or colour can also suggest a field of influence. Can something at one edge make a difference to how we see a mark at the other? The Library’s note gives the physical meaning of the word a place in that comparison. Field I · Field (Physics)

Reading note. Buddhism. In the Dvaya Sutta, visual consciousness arises in dependence on the eye and visible forms. The appearance of a painted field changes with the distance and position of the viewer. What belongs to the arrangement of marks, and what takes place in the encounter between that arrangement and the viewer? Dvaya Sutta, SN 35.93
